essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because their hydrophobic interior blocks many polar or charged substances.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move them against the gradient.
completionEvidence: Explain why a phospholipid bilayer is selectively permeable.

activities.label: Membrane model
activities.title: Phospholipid barrier model
activities.body: Study the membrane model and compare it to your own thinking.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because their hydrophobic interior blocks many polar or charged substances.

activities.label: Own words check
activities.title: Explain membrane selectivity
activities.body: In your own words, explain why the bilayer lets some substances pass more easily than others.
activities.correctAnswer: The hydrophobic interior of the phospholipid bilayer blocks many polar or charged substances, so only some substances cross easily.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links bilayer structure to what can cross and why. If missing, add the hydrophobic interior and the idea that it blocks polar or charged substances.

activities.label: Fix the transport rule
activities.title: Passive or active transport
activities.body: Repair your answer using the rule below, then give one corrected classification.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Treating passive transport as any movement across the membrane, even when energy is required.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves down a concentration gradient without energy; active transport uses energy to move against the gradient.
activities.feedback: The key repair is that energy use and direction relative to the gradient distinguish the two. Correct the classification by stating both parts together.

activities.label: Teach it back
activities.title: Transport from memory
activities.body: Explain the membrane model and the transport rule again without copying the model.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
activities.feedback: A complete response states both transport types and the difference in energy use and gradient direction.

activities.label: Quick recognition check
activities.title: Classify one transport example
activities.body: Choose the best classification for a substance moved into a cell against its gradient using energy.
choices: Passive transport
Active transport
Selective permeability
Simple diffusion only
activities.feedback: Using energy and moving against the gradient makes this active transport, not passive transport.

items.essentialIdea: Phospholipids form a bilayer with hydrophilic heads outward and hydrophobic tails inward.

check.title: Phospholipid orientation
check.prompt: How do phospholipid heads and tails arrange in a bilayer, and why does that matter for permeability?
check.referenceAnswer: Hydrophilic heads face the watery environments inside and outside the cell, while hydrophobic tails face inward away from water. This creates a barrier that limits passage of many polar or charged substances.
check.feedback: The inward hydrophobic core is what blocks many solutes, not the heads.

items.essentialIdea: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy.

check.title: Passive vs active transport
check.prompt: Why does passive transport not require energy, and what direction does it move substances?
check.referenceAnswer: Passive transport moves substances from higher to lower concentration, so it does not require cellular energy.
check.feedback: The key is movement down the gradient, not the use of a membrane protein.

recognitionCheck.title: Transport energy use
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement best describes passive transport?
choices: It moves substances from high to low concentration without cellular energy.
It moves substances from low to high concentration using cellular energy.
It moves only water through the membrane using ATP.
It stops when concentration is equal on both sides because proteins close the membrane.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: It moves substances from high to low concentration without cellular energy.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Passive transport goes down the gradient and does not use energy.
